heldSource.expression: tackles both the symptoms and the roots of the problem
heldSource.sentence: A good policy tackles both the symptoms and the roots of the problem.
heldSource.question: What can be done to alleviate poverty?
heldSource.sourceMeaning: Addresses immediate effects and underlying causes; medical and plant metaphors.

selectedOwner.title: treat the symptom rather than the cause
selectedOwner.sourceSentence: A short-term ban may treat the symptom rather than the cause.
selectedOwner.meaning: Respond to an outward effect or sign without addressing the underlying source.
senseOverlap: Both teach the immediate-effect versus underlying-cause distinction.
The 1104 brief explicitly allows useful temporary relief while the cause is investigated, so it does not force an either/or choice.

The owner listening and dialogue recommend both an immediate correction and removal of outdated schedules; the scene allows drying a wet floor while investigating the leak. These are positive two-track decisions similar to the held policy example.
selectedOwner.constructionDifference: The owner target criticizes a response that treats only the symptom; source 3860 praises a policy that tackles both the symptoms and the roots. It reverses the evaluation and mixes a medical image with roots as a plant image. It is not an inflected surface of the owner idiom.

assessmentCoverage.requiredForMerge: Revise brief grammar/Chinese and at least one assessed source-positive decision to distinguish tackle both from treat rather than, append exact provenance, use a reviewed bounded target union, update glossary forbidden/target spans, and rerun source-alias, six-key and audio-delta checks. Since this adds a second lexical construction, owner editorial approval is needed.

recommendation: Retain 3860 held at present. It is not a clear separate seven-step idiom because its source sentence is a transparent positive combination of familiar symptom/cause imagery, and the substantive causal decision is already taught by 1104. A careful two-construction expansion could support alias-existing, but a detector-only alias would misrepresent the current lesson and fail full-source coverage.
